t: The provisions of this Act are intended to supplement, and shall not be construed as limiting or repealing, existing legislation.

fable.w: This is a savings/construction clause stating that the Act supplements rather than limits or repeals existing legislation. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision. There is no real tempting opposite reading; nothing in the text is on-topic for participation.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard savings clause that clarifies the relationship between the new Act and existing laws. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. It contains no reference to public comment, advisory boards, hearings, or rights to sue.
qwen_block.s: The provisions of this Act are intended to supplement, and shall not be construed as limiting or repealing, existing legislation.

opus.w: This is a standard savings clause: it says the Act adds to existing law and does not limit or repeal it. It requires no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue that would involve anyone outside the federal government. Nothing in it is even about participation, so no quote is needed.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard savings clause that clarifies the relationship between the current Act and existing laws. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in federal decision-making. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The provisions of this Act are intended to supplement, and shall not be construed as limiting or repealing, existing legislation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "existing legislation" could involve participation mechanisms, so this section implicitly preserves them. However, the definition requires the section itself to *recommend or require* participation. This section is a savings clause that merely clarifies the scope of the Act relative to other laws; it does not establish any new process for outside parties to consult with or participate in federal decision-making.
